Package neqsim.thermodynamicoperations.propertygenerator

Class OLGApropertyTableGeneratorWaterKeywordFormat

java.lang.Object
neqsim.thermodynamicoperations.BaseOperation
neqsim.thermodynamicoperations.propertygenerator.OLGApropertyTableGeneratorWaterKeywordFormat
All Implemented Interfaces:
Serializable, Runnable, OperationInterface
public class OLGApropertyTableGeneratorWaterKeywordFormat extends BaseOperation
Generate three-phase OLGA keyword tables, with RS based on gas plus oil mass and standard liquid ratios including the separate aqueous phase. Optional bubble headers are omitted for multicomponent feeds; pure-component curves retain only validated saturation points.

    • fillAbsentPhaseNodes

      private void fillAbsentPhaseNodes()
      Extrapolate every phase-specific column into the nodes where that phase does not exist.

      OLGA rejects a table containing a zero gas, oil or water density, so nodes outside a phase's existence region are filled from the nearest node where it does exist, and a phase that exists nowhere falls back to a physical default. The phase mass fractions pin at zero there, so the extrapolated branch is never used in a flow calculation. With the monotonicity correction, density, enthalpy and entropy are first filled with the phase gradients so they stay monotonic and continuous across the phase boundary.

    • setEnvelopeRefinement

      public void setEnvelopeRefinement(boolean enabled, double factor)
      Concentrate range-axis points inside the water-free phase envelope.

      Along each axis whose envelope maximum (cricondenbar or cricondentherm) lies inside the range, a share gridFactor/(gridFactor+1) of the points is placed inside the envelope. Explicit axes are not changed.

      Parameters:
      enabled - true to refine
      factor - ratio of points inside to outside the envelope, 1 to 10
      Throws:
      IllegalArgumentException - if the factor is outside 1 to 10

    • setMonotonicityCorrection

      public void setMonotonicityCorrection(boolean correct)

      Parameters:
      correct - true to correct

    • setUseReferenceWaterProperties

      public void setUseReferenceWaterProperties(boolean use)
      Take aqueous density, its derivatives, heat capacity, enthalpy, entropy, viscosity and thermal conductivity from the IAPWS reference equations (IF97 Region 1, R12-08, R15-11) instead of the equation of state.

      Applied at nodes where the aqueous phase is at least 95 wt% water and inside 253.15-623.15 K and up to 1000 bara; other nodes keep the equation-of-state values, so inhibitor-rich water is not treated as pure water. Enthalpy and entropy are shifted to the equation-of-state reference at standard conditions, keeping latent heats consistent with the gas phase. Interfacial tensions are not changed.

      Parameters:
      use - true to use the reference equations

    • setWaterSalinity

      public void setWaterSalinity(double value, String unit)
      Set the salinity of the aqueous phase. Density, its derivatives and viscosity are corrected with the Batzle and Wang (1992) NaCl brine ratios; phase amounts and compositions are not affected. Not allowed for a feed that holds ionic components.
      Parameters:
      value - salinity value
      unit - "mg/l" (of solution at standard conditions), "ppm" (mg/kg solution), "wt%" or "kg/kg"
      Throws:
      IllegalArgumentException - if the unit is unknown or the value is out of range

      specification - "watercut" (volume % of the standard liquid), "mol/mol" (mol water per mol feed), "mol%" or "wt%" of feed plus water
